item.title: Cold-Chain Claims: Turning a Temperature Excursion into a Claim That Holds Up
item.description:
What is a cold-chain claim?

Quick answer

A cold-chain claim is a demand for money after a temperature-controlled load was spoiled or put at risk because it left its required temperature range in transit or in storage. It is made against the carrier, the warehouse or an insurer, depending on who had the goods and what the contract says.

The event behind it is called an excursion: a period when the load sat outside the range it was meant to stay in. A reefer unit that failed overnight. A door left open at a cross-dock. A pallet that waited on a warm dock before loading.

item.title: Freight Claims: How to File Loss, Damage and Shortage Claims Before the Window Closes
item.description:
What is a freight claim?

Quick answer

A freight claim is a written demand to a carrier for money, because goods were lost, damaged, short or delivered late while in the carrier’s care. It is how a shipper recovers the value of the goods and, where the contract allows, the cost of the delay. It only pays if it is filed in time and backed by records.

The trade calls the physical side OS&D: overage, shortage and damage. Something arrived that should not have, something did not arrive, or something arrived broken. Each one is a possible claim.

item.title: Revenue Leakage in Logistics: Where It Hides and How to Find Yours
item.description:
What is revenue leakage in logistics?

Quick answer

Revenue leakage in logistics is money a shipper was owed, or should never have paid, and did not get back. The usual sources are carrier overcharges, bills paid twice, damage and shortage claims left to expire, demurrage and detention on a held container, and orders that miss their window. It is almost always written down in your own systems before anyone acts on it.

Leakage is not one big loss. It is many small ones, each too small to chase on its own. A wrong fuel surcharge here. A liftgate fee for a delivery that had a dock. A crushed pallet nobody had the morning to claim. Each one is cheap to ignore and costly to add up.
